title: Neural circuit mechanisms for steering control in walking Drosophila
source_locator: Results, 'Contributions of single descending neuron types to steering behavior'; Figure 8A-C; Methods 'Stochastic ReaChR expression'
quote: In the flies with unilateral expression, we found that light evoked a small average steering bias in the ipsilateral direction
mapping_basis: Paper names the cell DNa02, a Namiki type name that type_list.csv lists as MANC type DNa02; line SS00730 maps to DNa02 in driver_lines.csv.
stimulation: 617 nm orange light from above the head, symmetric, 68 uW/mm2, 0.5 s every 11 s, 150 trials
sensory_condition: on spherical treadmill (air-supported ball), head cuticle intact, no dissection
coordination_notes: Only ball rotational velocity measured; legs not tracked.
penetrance: small average ipsilateral steering bias; mean outside 95% CI of bilateral-expression bootstrap null; individual flies variable (Fig. 8C)
n_flies_note: Figure 8B legend: mean of 16/17 flies (uni/bilateral ReaChR); Methods count 17 unilateral brains (9 left, 8 right) and 47 bilateral among 73 experiments.
notes: Flies walking on a treadmill were stimulated; the reported effect is an ipsilateral turning bias (rotational velocity peak about 50 deg/s), so leg-rhythm fields are not_assessed (turning in an already-walking fly, no leg tracking). Forward-velocity effects could not be attributed to DNa02 because of visual startle. 'Simulation' in the text is a bootstrap null, not a connectome model. Same experiment as in the bioRxiv version 10.1101/2020.04.04.024703.

title: Neural circuit mechanisms for steering control in walking Drosophila
source_locator: Results, 'Contributions of single descending neuron types to steering behavior' (paragraph after Figure 8 legend); Figure 8B-C (bilateral group)
quote: These effects were likely due to visual startle, because they were indistinguishable in flies with unilateral expression, bilateral expression, and no expression (data not shown).
mapping_basis: Paper names the cell DNa02, a Namiki type name that type_list.csv lists as MANC type DNa02; line SS00730 maps to DNa02 in driver_lines.csv.
stimulation: 617 nm orange light from above the head, symmetric, 68 uW/mm2, 0.5 s every 11 s, 150 trials
sensory_condition: on spherical treadmill (air-supported ball), head cuticle intact, no dissection
n_flies_note: Figure 8B legend: 17 bilateral flies; Methods report 47 brains with bilateral expression.
notes: Bilateral-expression siblings were used as controls. Their light-evoked forward-velocity changes were indistinguishable from no-expression flies (data not shown), which the authors attribute to visual startle. They say this dataset cannot show how DNa02 activation affects forward velocity. The rotational bias in Fig. 8B-C is null by construction because left/right labels were assigned at random. Legs were not tracked. Same experiment as in the bioRxiv version.
